# Design QA & Testing: Ensuring Quality Across Platforms

Implement comprehensive design QA workflows to validate quality, accessibility, consistency, and functionality across all devices and platforms.

## Overview

Design QA goes beyond visual review to ensure products are usable, accessible, consistent, performant, and meet specifications across all contexts.

## Responsive Design Testing

### Breakpoint Validation
- Test at documented breakpoints (mobile: 375px, tablet: 768px, desktop: 1440px)
- Verify layout adapts correctly at each breakpoint
- Check component spacing and sizing adjustments
- Ensure text remains readable at all sizes
- Test between breakpoints for reflow issues

### Mobile-First Review
- Start testing at smallest viewport first
- Verify touch targets minimum 44x44px
- Check vertical scroll experience without horizontal scroll
- Test all interactions at mobile size
- Validate modal and overlay behavior
- Review navigation pattern for mobile context

### Tablet and Landscape Testing
- Test at common tablet sizes (iPad, Android tablets)
- Review landscape orientation layouts
- Verify sufficient padding and margins
- Check two-column layouts work at tablet width
- Test split-view scenarios (email/detail on iPad)

### Desktop and Large Display
- Test at minimum and maximum supported widths
- Verify content width and line lengths (50-75 characters optimal)
- Check spacing doesn't feel excessive at large sizes
- Validate that stretched images don't distort
- Review navigation patterns for screen real estate

## Accessibility Testing

### Color Contrast
- WCAG AA: 4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large text
- WCAG AAA: 7:1 for normal text, 4.5:1 for large text
- Test with contrast checker tools
- Check background vs. text colors
- Verify focus indicators have sufficient contrast
- Test on various backgrounds, not just white

### Keyboard Navigation
- Tab through entire interface in logical order
- Verify all interactive elements are focusable
- Check focus indicators are visible and clear
- Test keyboard shortcuts for consistency
- Verify no keyboard traps (can't escape focus)
- Validate form navigation and submission

### Screen Reader Testing
- Use NVDA, JAWS, or VoiceOver to test
- Verify headings are properly structured (H1 > H2 > H3)
- Test alternative text on images describes content
- Validate form labels associated with inputs
- Check hidden elements marked appropriately
- Test link text makes sense out of context

### Semantic Structure
- Verify proper heading hierarchy without skipping levels
- Validate list structure for navigation and content
- Test form structure with label, input, error message relationships
- Check table headers and associations
- Verify landmarks used (main, nav, aside, footer)

## Cross-Browser Testing

### Browser Compatibility Matrix
- Chrome/Edge (Chromium-based): Latest 2 versions
- Firefox: Latest 2 versions
- Safari: Latest 2 versions (macOS and iOS)
- Test interaction patterns, animations, gradients
- Verify CSS and layout rendering consistency

### Rendering Verification
- Check typography rendering across browsers
- Verify shadow and gradient quality
- Test animation smoothness and performance
- Check transparency and blend modes
- Validate form input styling and behavior

### Feature Detection
- Test features that might not be supported uniformly
- CSS Grid, Flexbox, custom properties
- Backdrop filters, mix-blend-mode
- Modern font features (variable fonts)
- Verify graceful degradation if unsupported

## Performance and Visual Quality

### Image Quality
- Verify images don't appear blurry or pixelated
- Check image dimensions match intended size
- Test responsive image sizes (srcset)
- Validate retina/2x display rendering
- Review image compression doesn't degrade quality

### Animation Performance
- Test animations remain smooth (60fps target)
- Verify no jank or stuttering
- Check animation duration and timing feel natural
- Validate animations complete without hanging
- Test on various device performance levels (throttle CPU)

### Loading States
- Verify all loading indicators appear promptly
- Test skeleton screens and placeholders
- Check error states display appropriately
- Validate timeout handling and messaging
- Test network throttle scenarios

## Consistency Verification

### Design System Compliance
- Verify spacing follows grid system
- Check typography uses defined sizes and weights
- Validate colors match design system palette
- Confirm components use approved patterns
- Check for any ad-hoc styling that bypasses system

### Component Consistency
- Test buttons look and behave consistently
- Verify form inputs are uniform across product
- Check card layouts maintain consistent spacing
- Validate modal and dialog styling
- Review header/footer consistency

### Brand Consistency
- Verify brand colors are correct and consistent
- Check logo usage and sizing
- Validate typography matches brand guidelines
- Review imagery style and tone
- Check overall visual cohesion

## Content and Copy Review

### Typography Quality
- Check for orphaned words (single word on new line)
- Verify no excessive hyphenation
- Test long content without line breaks
- Check punctuation and spacing (em dashes, ellipsis)
- Review line lengths for readability (50-75 chars optimal)

### Placeholder and Error Content
- Test all error message states display correctly
- Verify placeholder text provides helpful guidance
- Check empty states have meaningful messaging
- Test very long content in input/output areas
- Validate special characters display properly

### Copy Length and Translations
- Test content at different text lengths
- Verify layouts work with longer text (translations)
- Check right-to-left language support if applicable
- Test multi-line content behavior
- Validate truncation with ellipsis appropriate

## Form and Interaction Testing

### Form Validation
- Test required field validation
- Verify error messages appear near relevant fields
- Check success states after submission
- Test field-level validation on blur/change
- Validate form state preservation on error

### Button and Link Behavior
- Verify disabled buttons appear appropriately
- Test loading/processing button states
- Check link underlines and hover states clear
- Validate focus states on all interactive elements
- Test click/touch targets sized appropriately

### Dropdowns and Selections
- Test dropdown open/close behavior
- Verify selected state displays clearly
- Check dropdown position (doesn't go off-screen)
- Test keyboard navigation in dropdowns
- Validate scroll behavior in long lists

## Data and State Testing

### Empty States
- Design and review empty state layouts
- Verify messaging is clear and helpful
- Check empty state doesn't break layout
- Test CTA for actionable next steps
- Validate visual hierarchy in empty state

### Loading States
- Test all loading indicator styles
- Verify loading duration matches actual time
- Check content replacement or overlay
- Test skeleton screens vs. spinners
- Validate loading messaging

### Error and Warning States
- Test error message styling and placement
- Verify warning states are visually distinct
- Check inline vs. notification errors
- Test dismissible error handling
- Validate error recovery path

## QA Checklist

### Visual QA
- [ ] Spacing consistent with design system
- [ ] Typography matches specifications
- [ ] Colors accurate to palette
- [ ] Images sharp and appropriately scaled
- [ ] Alignment perfect (grid, centering)
- [ ] No visual bugs (clipping, overflow)

### Functional QA
- [ ] All interactions work as designed
- [ ] Forms validate and submit correctly
- [ ] Links navigate to correct locations
- [ ] Buttons trigger appropriate actions
- [ ] Modals open and close properly

### Accessibility QA
- [ ] Color contrast meets WCAG AA minimum
- [ ] Keyboard navigation works end-to-end
- [ ] Screen readers describe content accurately
- [ ] Focus indicators visible throughout
- [ ] No keyboard traps

### Responsiveness QA
- [ ] Tested at 3+ breakpoints
- [ ] Touch targets minimum 44x44px
- [ ] No horizontal scroll at mobile
- [ ] Text readable without zoom
- [ ] Landscape and portrait work

### Content QA
- [ ] Copy accurate and properly spell-checked
- [ ] No orphaned words or excessive hyphenation
- [ ] Placeholder and error messages clear
- [ ] Links work and point to correct pages
- [ ] Numbers and dates formatted correctly

## Documentation and Handoff

### QA Report
- Document all issues found with screenshots
- Categorize as critical, high, medium, low
- Provide reproduction steps for each issue
- Suggest fixes or improvements
- Track status until resolved

### Sign-Off Process
- Define QA acceptance criteria
- Get stakeholder approval before launch
- Document any known limitations
- Create post-launch monitoring plan
- Schedule post-launch follow-up review

## Best Practices

- Create detailed QA checklist per project
- Test on real devices, not just browser emulation
- Involve actual users in usability testing
- Automate repetitive visual regression tests
- Document edge cases and workarounds
- Test early and often throughout design process
- Balance perfection with ship-ability

## Common Pitfalls

- Testing only on latest devices and browsers
- Assuming mobile-responsive means accessible
- Not testing keyboard navigation thoroughly
- Skipping QA to meet deadlines
- Not involving accessibility specialists
- Testing in isolation without user feedback
- Assuming developers will catch design issues

faqs.question: What's the difference between accessibility testing and QA?
faqs.answer: QA ensures the product works as designed and meets specifications (visual, functional, responsive). Accessibility testing specifically verifies the product is usable by people with disabilities (keyboard navigation, screen readers, contrast, semantic structure). Both are essential—QA catches bugs, accessibility testing ensures inclusion.

faqs.question: Should I test on real devices or is browser emulation sufficient?
faqs.answer: Test on real devices when possible, especially for mobile. Browser emulation misses real-world factors: actual touch behavior, OS-level navigation, network conditions, device performance. At minimum, emulate; ideally test on at least one real phone and tablet per major OS (iOS, Android).

faqs.question: How do I prioritize QA issues when there are many?
faqs.answer: Categorize by severity: Critical (blocking functionality), High (major impact, workaround exists), Medium (noticeable but doesn't break usage), Low (polish/refinement). Fix critical first, then high, then medium before launch. Low issues can move to post-launch roadmap.

faqs.question: What should I include in a QA checklist?
faqs.answer: Cover: Visual (spacing, typography, colors, alignment), Functional (interactions work as designed), Accessibility (contrast, keyboard, screen reader), Responsive (multiple breakpoints, touch targets), Content (accuracy, spelling, formatting), and Browser/Device coverage. Customize based on project specifics.
